transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this. 

I guess I'm just having a little trouble... well, I just can't seem to keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. It's probably not a huge deal, but it's starting to affect my work, even when it's something really important. I do computer support, and... well, it's a bit embarrassing to admit, but I'll start tracing a client's network problem, and ten minutes later I'll realize I've reread the exact same log entries three times. And I still have absolutely no idea what they actually say. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.
Do you feel anxious or overwhelmed when you're trying to focus on a task?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say anxious. I don't think so, anyway. I really don't want to make it sound like I can't handle the job or that I'm stressed out, because I'm really not. The work itself is fine, and I like my team. 

It's just... I just kind of drift off, I guess? It's definitely not a panic thing or feeling overwhelmed by the difficulty of the task. I just sort of lose the thread. I hope that makes sense. Is that... is that a helpful answer? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you find that you have trouble focusing at any particular time of day?

Hmm, time of day... you know, I really haven't noticed a specific time. I hope that's an okay answer. I mean, it just sort of... happens whenever. 

Morning, afternoon, it doesn't seem to make much of a difference. I could be looking at a support ticket at 9 AM or 3 PM and it's just the same sort of drifting. I really wish I could give you a better pattern to work with. Am I supposed to be tracking that? I can definitely start keeping a log if that would make things easier for you to figure out! I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. Did that answer the question alright?
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?

Oh, um... well, maybe a little? I mean, I try really hard not to be disruptive or anything. But I guess... well, if I'm sitting with a client, or, um, I go to these chess meetings, and I'll suddenly realize my leg is just bouncing away. Or I'll be clicking a pen, or... twisting a little plastic cable tie around in my fingers. 

I usually don't even notice I'm doing it until somebody finally gives me that... that look, you know? Like I'm being a distraction. I always stop right away when they do, I promise! I really don't want to bother anyone, and it's just a nervous habit, really. 

Is that... does that count as fidgeting? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. Did that answer your question okay?
Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they finish speaking?

Oh, gosh... um. I really try not to be rude, I promise. I know how important it is to let people finish, especially at work. But... well, sometimes, yes. 

It happens a lot when we're having tech discussions, or when a user is explaining an issue to me. The answer just sort of... jumps right into my head, you know? And before I can stop myself, I'm already talking over them, or... or even reaching over to grab their keyboard to just fix it while they're still talking. 

I always feel terrible right after, and I apologize immediately. I don't mean to be disrespectful or make them feel unheard. It's just that the solution is right there, and it just sort of bursts out of me. 

Does that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible person to work with. I'm trying to get better at it, I really am. Was that a helpful answer?
Do you often act on impulse when you're not talking to someone, like doing something sudden without thinking it through?

Oh, um... impulse? Like, doing things without thinking... gosh, I hope I don't do that too much. I try really hard to be deliberate about things, especially at my age. You'd think I'd have all that sorted out by now, right? 

But, um... when I'm just on my own? I don't know, I guess I'm pretty normal in that regard. I mean, I don't go out and buy sports cars on a whim or anything crazy like that! Maybe I'll occasionally start a new project at home when I should be doing something else, but... I think everybody does that sometimes, don't they? 

I really haven't noticed anything major. I hope that's the right kind of answer. If there's something specific you mean, I can try to think harder on it! I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is that okay?
Do you often find that you leave tasks unfinished, even when you know you need to complete them?

Oh... gosh. Well, to be perfectly honest, this is actually sort of the main reason I decided to come in and see you. I'm a little embarrassed to admit it, because I really do pride myself on doing a good job, but... yes. I've been having a really hard time keeping my mind on a task long enough to actually finish it anymore. Even when I know it's incredibly important. 

Like, um... I'll sit down to trace a client's network problem, and I'll be trying so hard to just get it done. But then ten minutes will go by, and I'll suddenly realize I've just reread the exact same log entries three times in a row, and I still have no idea what they actually say. 

It's so frustrating, and I feel terrible about it. I really don't want my boss or the clients to think I'm slacking off or incompetent, because I promise I'm trying my absolute best to just finish my work. Is that... does that answer what you were asking? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you often feel emotionally overwhelmed or have intense mood swings?

Oh, um... emotionally overwhelmed? Gosh, I really try not to let things get to me. I mean, I like to think of myself as a pretty even-keeled guy, especially at work. You kind of have to be when you're dealing with frustrated people and broken computers all day, right? 

I really don't think I have intense mood swings or anything like that. I mean, sure, I get a little stressed sometimes when the ticket queue gets backed up, but... I don't go flying off the handle or breaking down crying or anything dramatic. I try really hard to keep a positive attitude and just push through. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm hiding anything! I just really haven't noticed my emotions being a big problem. I want to be as helpful as possible, though—is there a specific kind of reaction you're looking for? I can try to think of an example if that would help you more. Did I answer that okay?
Have you always had trouble focusing and sitting still, or is this something that has developed more recently?

Oh, um... always? Gosh, I don't want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, because I really did try to be good! But, well... I suppose it's not entirely new. 

I mean, my mother... she actually still jokes about it sometimes. She says that back in grade school, my report cards would always say I was a bright boy, which was nice of the teachers to say! But, um... they also said I never stayed in my seat, and I guess I had a bad habit of blurting out answers before I was called on. Oh, and I apparently lost my homework a lot, even when I had actually done it. 

I'm a little embarrassed to admit all that, honestly. I'd like to think I've matured a lot since then! But I guess... yeah, I suppose the trouble with focusing and being a bit fidgety has kind of always been there in the background. I just really hope I haven't been too much of a bother to people because of it. Is that the kind of history you needed to know? I hope I'm giving you the right details.
Have you had to make any significant changes to your daily routine or work habits because of these focusing and fidgeting issues?

Oh, um... changes? Well... gosh, I really hate to admit this, because I always want to be someone people can rely on. I try so hard to be dependable, I really do. But... yes, things have changed quite a bit lately. 

I used to have a very structured job, and that seemed to help keep me on track. But since I lost that structure... well, I've had to try and manage things on my own with freelance work, and I'm afraid it hasn't gone as smoothly as I'd hoped. I'm so embarrassed to say this, but my reputation has taken a bit of a hit. I've actually lost a few freelance clients because... well, because I couldn't seem to get the work done when I said I would. 

And, um, there was a senior service-manager role I was really hoping for, but I missed out on it. I think people are just having a hard time trusting me to follow through on things right now, which is just an awful feeling. I never want to let anyone down. It's even gotten to the point where my wife and I have had to worry about money a little bit, which makes me feel terrible as a husband. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds really bad. I promise I'm not trying to make excuses, and I'm really motivated to get back on track! I just... I want to be completely honest with you so you can help me. Did I explain that alright? I hope I'm not coming across as irresponsible.
Do you ever find yourself becoming extremely focused on a task, to the point where you lose track of everything else around you?

Oh, um... extremely focused? Like, losing track of everything else? Gosh, I really don't think I do that. I mean, I try to be very attentive to my surroundings and the people I'm working with. I wouldn't want to ignore anyone or make them feel like they aren't important! 

I suppose there are times when I'm working on a really tricky computer issue and I get, you know, engaged in trying to fix it. I want to do a good job for the client, so I put my head down and work hard. But I wouldn't say I get... lost in it, or forget about the world. I try really hard to stay aware of what's going on around me, especially since my wife might need me for something, or a client might call. 

I hope that's the right kind of answer! I just haven't really noticed myself zoning out like that. I always try to be present and available. Does that make sense, or did you mean something different? I can try to think harder if I'm not giving you what you need.
Did your parents or teachers ever mention that you had trouble paying attention or sitting still when you were a child?

Oh, um... yes, actually. I think we might have touched on this just a little bit earlier, but... gosh, I hope you don't mind me repeating myself! I want to make sure I'm answering your question properly. 

But yes, my mother... she actually still jokes about it to this day, which is a little embarrassing, but she means well! She always brings up how, back in grade school, my report cards would always say I was a bright boy. I really did try my best to be a good student! But, well... the teachers also wrote that I never stayed in my seat, and that I had a habit of blurting out answers before it was my turn. Oh, and apparently I lost my homework quite a bit, even when I had spent the time doing it. 

I really hate thinking that I was a difficult child for my teachers to manage. I always wanted to be helpful and polite! But I guess those things were definitely noticed back then. Does that help answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of background information.
Did your trouble with focusing and sitting still start when you were a child or did it develop later in life?

Well, um... I guess, like I was just saying with my mom's stories, those little quirks have probably been around since I was a boy. But I always tried so hard to keep it all together, you know? I really did my best to compensate so it wouldn't affect anyone else. 

But as far as it being a real problem... gosh, it's so hard to admit this. The really serious trouble only started about... oh, a year and ten months ago. That's when I... well, I was let go from my old job. I'm so embarrassed to even say the word "fired" out loud, because I truly pride myself on being a dedicated worker. I hope you don't think less of me for that. 

It's just that when I lost that position, I lost all the external systems and the daily structure that used to keep me on track. Without that framework, everything just sort of unraveled over this past year and ten months. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining the timeline okay for you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to understand the whole picture!
Have you ever been diagnosed with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder or taken any medication for it?

Oh, um... no, I've never been diagnosed with anything like that. And I've certainly never taken any medication for it! 

I mean, I've always just tried to work hard and push through things on my own, you know? I wouldn't want to take up a doctor's time with something I should be able to manage myself. I've always felt like if I just tried a little harder, made a few more lists, or set a few more alarms, I could keep everything running smoothly. I really don't want to be a burden or rely on pills if I don't absolutely have to. 

I hope it's okay that I haven't seen anyone about this before now. I just always thought it was a personal failing I needed to work on, rather than something medical. Does that seem reasonable? I really hope I'm not making things more difficult for you by not having a previous diagnosis on record.
Do you often feel restless or have an inability to engage in activities quietly in your daily life?

Oh, um... well, I suppose sometimes I do have a little trouble with that. I mean, I really try my best to be respectful and attentive, especially when someone is talking to me or when I'm in a meeting. I know how important it is to be a good listener! 

But, gosh, it's hard to explain without sounding like I'm just being rude or impatient, which I promise I'm not trying to be! It's just that... even when I know I'm supposed to sit still and listen, it sometimes feels like there's this little motor humming right under my skin. It's almost like a physical urge where I feel like I just need to stand up, or maybe check something on my computer, or just move on to the next problem right that very second. 

I really try to keep it hidden, though! I'll tap my foot quietly or just grip my pen a little tighter so I don't disrupt anyone. I hope that doesn't make me sound too difficult to be around. Do you think that's the kind of restlessness you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Have your focusing and fidgeting issues caused problems in your personal relationships, such as with your wife or friends?

Oh, um... well, my wife is incredibly patient, she really is. I don't want to make it sound like I'm a bad husband or anything! But... I guess it has caused some stress between us lately. It's really hard to talk about because I'm just so ashamed of it, to be honest. 

Since losing the structure of my old job, my... well, my professional reputation has taken a real hit. I've been trying to keep things afloat, but I've actually lost some freelance clients, and... oh, this is hard to say... I recently missed out on a senior service-manager role that I really should have been able to get. It seems like people just... they feel like they can't trust me to follow through on things right now. 

Because of all those missed opportunities, my wife and I have had to really worry about money, which just breaks my heart. I want to be a good, reliable partner for her, you know? I'm trying so hard to get back on track so she doesn't have to stress about our finances. I hope I'm not painting too terrible a picture of myself... I really am trying my best to fix things. Does that answer what you were asking about how it affects my relationships?
Have you experienced difficulties with focusing and sitting still consistently throughout your adult life, not just in the past year and ten months?

Oh, um... well, yes, I suppose it's not entirely a new thing. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I've been a mess my whole life! I've always tried really hard to be good and do what's expected of me. 

But, gosh, if I'm being completely honest... it has kind of always been there. Even back when I was a kid. My mother actually still jokes about it sometimes, which is a little embarrassing. She says that back in grade school, my report cards always had these notes from the teachers saying I was a bright boy, but... well, that I just couldn't seem to stay in my seat. And apparently, I had a habit of blurting out answers before I was called on. Oh, and losing my homework, even when I had actually done it! 

I guess I've always had to work a little extra hard to keep things organized and keep myself focused. I just always thought it was something I'd eventually outgrow or learn to manage better if I just applied myself more. I hope it doesn't make me sound like I've been irresponsible my whole life. Does that help answer your question about how long this has been going on?
Do you think your difficulties with focusing and fidgeting are more related to inattention, hyperactivity, or a combination of both?

Oh, um... gosh, that's a really good question. I want to make sure I give you the right answer, but... well, I'm honestly not entirely sure how to separate them. I don't want to sound like I'm making excuses or anything! 

I guess... maybe it's a bit of both? I mean, I really do try so hard to pay attention, I promise I do. But sometimes the thoughts just slip away, or I get distracted, which I suppose is the inattention part. And then, like I mentioned before, there's that feeling of needing to move or tap my foot, which I guess is the other part. 

I don't know if one is worse than the other, really. They just kind of... happen together, I think? I hope that's an okay answer. I just want to be as helpful as possible so we can figure this out. Does that make sense, or did you need me to try and pick one over the other?
Did you experience significant difficulties with focusing and sitting still as a child?

Oh, um... well, yes, I think we touched on this just a moment ago, actually. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details. 

But yes, as a child... it was definitely there. I really was a good kid, I promise, I never meant to cause trouble! But my mother, she still likes to tease me about it sometimes. She says my grade school report cards always had these notes from my teachers. They would say I was a very bright boy, which was nice of them, but... well, that I just couldn't ever seem to stay in my seat. And apparently, I was always blurting out answers before it was my turn to speak. 

Oh, and the homework... gosh, that was the most frustrating part. I would actually do the work, I really would, but then I'd somehow lose it before I could turn it in. I always felt so bad about it. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a terrible student! I really did try my best to be good. Is that the kind of information you were looking for about my childhood?
Did you experience any of these focusing or fidgeting issues before you started school?

Oh, um... before school? Gosh, that's going back quite a ways... I'm 53 now, so it's a little fuzzy, to be perfectly honest. I don't want to give you the wrong answer. 

I don't... think so? I mean, my mother never really mentioned anything about me being a difficult toddler or anything like that. I think I was just a normal, happy little boy, you know? Just playing and doing regular kid things. The stories she tells are mostly about once I got into a classroom setting where I had to sit at a desk all day. 

I hope it's okay that I don't remember much from back then. I really wish I had a better memory for those early years to help you out more. Does that make sense, or should I try to think a little harder about it?
